title: Undo puts each line back to the technician it had; an empty line stays empty
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 20 minutes.
  • Build: the QA branch for the Undo fast follow, sv11567 (https://sv11567.qa.shopview.com).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • Two eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] "Ralph Edwards" and [Tech-B] "Dana Ortiz". A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" (used by this case only) with one work order [WO-1], created on this build, Approved, no lead technician, with three lines: Line 1 Unassigned (no technician) · Line 2 Explicit (its own technician [Tech-B]) · Line 3 Complete (no technician, status Complete).
  • The technician names are used in the expected results and stay as written; the line names are only labels and the number is an example.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Ralph Edwards" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] = "Dana Ortiz" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Line names in this case (such as "Line 1") are only labels for you: the New Line form's "What Are You Doing?" box only offers ready-made lines (typed text finds no results), so pick any ready-made line for each one (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot") and write down which is which.
  6. Create a new work order on this build for "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" with no lead technician: Work Orders > Create Work Order > pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Record its number as [WO-1] (e.g. "S1-710").
    • Add "Line 1 Unassigned" with no technician.
    • Add "Line 2 Explicit" and in Edit Line set Technicians = [Tech-B].
    • Add "Line 3 Complete" with no technician, approve it, enter a tech story and complete it.
    • Approve the other lines (the work order reads Approved).
    • Write down each line's Labor row: Line 1 Unassigned, Line 2 [Tech-B], Line 3 Unassigned (Complete).
  7. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" shows [WO-1] in the Unassigned column (Board View) with status Approved; its Lines tab matches what you wrote down. If not, fix the line or create a fresh work order before starting; then clear the search.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" in Search.
  3. Drag the [WO-1] card from the Unassigned column onto Ralph Edwards' column and let go.
  4. Before the message closes (about 5 seconds), click "Undo" on the message.
  5. Click the [WO-1] card to open the work order, open the Lines tab and read each line's Labor row.
  6. Go back to Work Orders (Board View, the same search) and drag the [WO-1] card from Unassigned onto Ralph Edwards' column again. This time do not click Undo.
  7. Open [WO-1] again, open the Lines tab and read each line's Labor row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

The PRD rule this test checks, word for word (S4-R32): “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Each labor line goes back to the technician it had before the change, and a line that had none goes back to none; Undo does not apply the S4-R8 line rules. Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Move the work order back by hand.” shows.”

  • Step 3: the card moves to Ralph Edwards' column and the message "[WO-1] assigned to Ralph Edwards" shows (e.g. "S1-710 assigned to Ralph Edwards"), with "Undo".
  • Step 4: the message closes, the card goes back to the Unassigned column and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button.
  • Step 5: the lines are exactly as before the change: Line 1 reads Unassigned (no technician), Line 2 still shows Dana Ortiz, Line 3 (Complete) still reads Unassigned.
  • Step 7: Line 1 now shows Ralph Edwards, Line 2 still shows Dana Ortiz, Line 3 still reads Unassigned. This shows the lead change does move Line 1, so step 5 proves Undo put it back.

Known problem (SV-11567, in Code Review on 28 Oct 2026, fast follow; Undo is its own ticket, Chris Ward on SV-11524, 20 Oct 2026; seen on the QA branch sv11524 on 26 Oct 2026): the message has the right words but no "Undo" button, only a close (×), and it closes after about 2.6 seconds. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, Undo has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Each labor line goes back to the technician it had before the change, and a line that had none goes back to none; Undo does not apply the S4-R8 line rules. Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change.   • S4-R8 table: Complete: “Status is Complete | No”
